source: A commonplace book: short quotations and questions for the table. Used when no notebook has been loaded.

items.text: Our life is frittered away by detail. Simplify, simplify.
items.author: Henry David Thoreau

items.text: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.
items.author: Henry David Thoreau

items.text: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
items.author: Marcus Aurelius

items.text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
items.author: Seneca

items.text: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
items.author: Seneca

items.text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
items.author: Seneca

items.text: Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year.
items.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

items.text: The years teach much which the days never know.
items.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

items.text: Well done is better than well said.
items.author: Benjamin Franklin

items.text: One today is worth two tomorrows.
items.author: Benjamin Franklin

items.text: Who was kind to you this week, and how could you be kind back?
What is something you're getting better at?
If our family had a motto, what would it be?
What was the best part of your day, and what was the hardest part?
